summary: Full backend + frontend testing of MASCI Job Site Safety Inspection app. 8/8 backend pytest tests passed. End-to-end UI flow (create -> view -> dashboard list -> delete) verified successfully including signature drawing on canvas, conditional sections, YES/NO toggles, validation, print, and delete from both detail page and dashboard.
critical_code_review_comments: server.py: list_inspections projection includes 'photos' just to compute photo_count -- with base64 photos in DB this can produce large network reads. Consider a Mongo aggregation with $size on photos to avoid pulling photo bytes for the listing endpoint as the dataset grows.
server.py: InspectionCreate uses extra='allow' which is permissive; acceptable here given the conditional schema, but consider stricter validation for top-level keys to prevent payload bloat.

Storing base64 photos and signatures inline in MongoDB documents will hit the 16MB BSON document limit if users upload many photos; for production, consider GridFS or object storage with referenced URLs. PhotoUpload.jsx already compresses, but this should be documented.

Frontend: The sub-checklist row testid pattern is `${sec.key}-row-${item.key}` while the per-item YesNo testid is `${sec.key}-${item.key}` - consistent and good. PPE/hazard testids follow `ppe-row-*`/`hazard-row-*` for rows and `ppe-*`/`hazard-*` for toggles. All interactive elements have data-testid as required.
ViewInspection has no explicit handling for an inspection with `_id` fields if any older docs exist; backend already strips _id on all responses so this is fine.
NewInspection.jsx (>500 lines) is large but cohesive. Could be split into per-section subcomponents for maintainability.
seed_data_creation: Tests create and clean up TEST_-prefixed inspections; no seed data left behind.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Backend pytest suite at /app/backend/tests/test_inspections.py covers all CRUD paths (POST, GET list, GET by id, DELETE, 404s, _id exclusion). Frontend signature canvases require real mouse drag with delays between moves (page.mouse.move/down/up + ~15ms waits between intermediate moves) for react-signature-canvas to register strokes; dispatching synthetic PointerEvents via JS does NOT work. End-to-end UI test flow created an inspection (id captured from URL), verified dashboard list and delete; the test cleans up after itself.
rca of the issue: No active issues. During testing, dispatching synthetic PointerEvents to draw on the signature canvas did not trigger react-signature-canvas's onEnd handler (the underlying signature_pad library treats synthetic events without proper pointer capture as non-strokes). Resolution: use Playwright's real page.mouse with multi-step move + small wait_for_timeout delays between moves, which produced valid strokes and allowed full e2e submission.
